events.title: Exercise Azure Shield
events.text: The Eastern Theater Command proposes its largest exercise yet: live-fire zones on every side of Taiwan, carrier groups east of the island and rehearsals of a customs blockade.

options.text: Hold the exercise at full scale

events.title: Readiness in the strait
events.text: Warships and drones crowd the median line. The cabinet must decide how loudly to answer.

options.text: Raise readiness and call up reservists

events.title: The customs quarantine
events.text: Planners propose a "law-enforcement quarantine": coast guard cutters would inspect every ship bound for Taiwan, a blockade in all but name that dares others to fire first.

events.title: Answering the quarantine
events.text: Chinese coast guard cutters are boarding freighters bound for Taiwan. Allies in Tokyo and Manila ask what Washington will do.

events.title: Standoff in the strait
events.text: Escorted convoys sail toward Kaohsiung through the inspection zone. Any boarding now means firing on foreign warships.

options.text: Let the convoys pass and open talks

events.title: The silicon shield
events.text: Allies press Taiwan's chipmakers to build their most advanced fabs abroad, in case the strait closes.

options.text: Keep the leading-edge fabs at home

events.title: Collision at the shoal
events.text: A Chinese coast guard cutter rams a Philippine supply boat at a disputed shoal in the South China Sea. Sailors are injured and the boat is towed away.

events.title: Suitors for Greenland
events.text: As the ice retreats, rare-earth and uranium deposits draw offers from Washington, Beijing and Brussels. The young state must choose its partners.

options.text: A security and investment pact with the United States

events.title: Chinese mines in Greenland
events.text: Greenland has signed mining concessions with Chinese firms a few hundred kilometres from the Pituffik radar base.

options.text: Outbid them with aid and a defence pact

events.title: The Northern Sea Route opens
events.text: For the first time cargo ships can cross the Arctic along the Siberian coast for most of the year. Moscow regards the route as internal waters.

options.text: Charge tolls and require Russian escorts
Open the route to all with Chinese partners

events.title: Incident off Svalbard
events.text: A Russian frigate shadows a Norwegian survey ship near Svalbard and jams its navigation. Oslo must decide how to answer in the High North.

options.text: Reinforce the north with allied patrols
Seek a fisheries and safety deal with Moscow

events.title: The Arctic seabed
events.text: Russian, Danish and Canadian claims to the Arctic seabed overlap along the Lomonosov Ridge, and Russian icebreakers have been seen in the Northwest Passage.

events.title: Severed cables
events.text: Two undersea data cables and a gas pipeline in the Baltic have been cut by a dragged anchor. The freighter belongs to a shadow fleet of untraceable owners.

options.text: Blame Moscow and board shadow-fleet ships

events.title: Exercise West-35
events.text: The General Staff wants a strategic exercise in Belarus and Kaliningrad rehearsing the closure of the Suwałki corridor between them.

options.text: Hold the exercise at full scale

events.title: The Eastern Shield
events.text: Russian divisions are exercising a few kilometres from the border. The government can finish the Eastern Shield fortifications or ask allies for more troops.

events.title: Attack in Kashmir
events.text: A deadly attack on a convoy in Kashmir is blamed on militants based across the Line of Control. Television studios demand retaliation.

events.title: Strikes across the line
events.text: Indian missiles and drones have struck targets across the Line of Control. Both arsenals are on alert and foreign capitals are calling.

events.title: The hotline
events.text: Pakistan has answered with strikes of its own, and both militaries have dispersed their missile units. The directors of military operations are on the hotline.

options.text: Agree a ceasefire and new confidence measures

events.title: The Indus waters
events.text: With the glaciers shrinking and the 1960 treaty in abeyance, new dams upstream threaten the flow that feeds Punjab and Sindh.

options.text: Take the case to international arbitration
Declare that diverting the rivers is an act of war

events.title: At the threshold
events.text: Iran has enough enriched uranium for several weapons and the know-how to build them. The leadership debates whether to cross the line.

options.text: Stay a threshold state and bargain
Accept intrusive inspections for sanctions relief

events.title: A nuclear Iran
events.text: Intelligence services conclude that Iran has assembled its first nuclear weapons.

options.text: Declare a red line and rely on deterrence

events.title: Tanker seized at Hormuz
events.text: Revolutionary Guard speedboats can seize a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s oil still passes, as leverage against sanctions.

events.title: Escorts in the Gulf
events.text: Shipping insurers have suspended cover for the Gulf and oil prices are soaring.

options.text: Leave it to the Gulf states

events.title: Mines in the strait
events.text: American warships are turning Iranian tankers away. Commanders propose to mine the strait.

events.title: Heat dome over the Gulf
events.text: Temperatures above 50 °C for weeks on end shut down outdoor work and strain the power grids and desalination plants.

options.text: Fund cooling, shade and night shifts

events.title: Drought on the Nile
events.text: A multi-year drought in the Ethiopian highlands has cut the flood. Ethiopia keeps filling its reservoirs and Lake Nasser is falling.

options.text: Ration water and build desalination plants

events.title: The Nile ultimatum
events.text: Cairo demands guaranteed releases from the dam during droughts, backed by Sudan.

options.text: Refuse: the river is ours too

events.title: War council in Cairo
events.text: Ethiopia has rejected any binding releases. Some generals argue that only force will keep the Nile flowing.

events.title: Talks on the Red Sea war
events.text: African Union mediators propose a ceasefire with Eritrea: a guaranteed transit corridor to the port of Assab in exchange for withdrawal.

events.title: Transition deadline
events.text: The ruling junta’s promised return to civilian rule falls due again, while insurgents hold much of the countryside.

events.title: The Essequibo claim
events.text: Guyana’s offshore oil boom has made the long-disputed Essequibo region one of the richest stretches of the Caribbean coast.

options.text: Press the claim in words and maps

events.title: Spy satellites from Sohae
events.text: Engineers are ready to launch a cluster of reconnaissance satellites on a new heavy rocket.

events.title: Arms control in Geneva
events.text: With no treaty limiting strategic arsenals since 2026, negotiators propose a framework to cap deployed warheads.

options.text: Build up to match China as well

events.title: Q-Day
events.text: Our quantum laboratory has broken a widely used public-key cipher. Years of intercepted traffic could now be read.

options.text: Keep it secret and read the archives
Announce it and lead the move to new ciphers

events.title: Super-cyclone in the delta
events.text: A super-cyclone and a record storm surge sweep across the coastal districts. Millions are homeless and fields are flooded with salt water.
